preamble: Diphthongization of the high front vowel [i] (usually long [iː]) to [ei], the first step of a lowering path that often continues to [ai]. Cantonese vernacular readings turn Middle Chinese -ij into -ei (四 sijH > sei3). Common Czech ej for Old Czech ý (malej 'small') is not filed here: Wiktionary gives the 15th-century pronunciation of malý as /ˈmaliː/ or /ˈmalaj/, and the new diphthong was first written ay (Czech Wikipedia, Diftongizace), so an aj stage is recorded. Czech aj > ej is filed under [ai] > [ei].

examples.note: Vernacular reading; the rare literary reading si3 /siː³³/ preserves the monophthong.
